items.statement: If a perfectoid K-algebra B is a finite étale extension of a sub-K-algebra A, then A is perfectoid: one reduces to the Galois case and applies Proposition 3.8.1 on invariants. André notes this partial converse is not used in the sequel.

items.name: Extremal quotients of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid
items.statement: The embedding K-Perf → K-uBan is faithful with a right adjoint, so it preserves and reflects epimorphisms. Since K-Perf is coreflective with monomorphic adjunction counits, it is stable under extremal quotients: for B perfectoid and φ:B→C an extremal epimorphism of uniform Banach K-algebras, C is perfectoid — though viewed as an epimorphism of perfectoid algebras φ need not be extremal.

items.name: A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid
items.statement: For A a spectral perfectoid K-algebra and g∈A°, the canonical A⊗̂_K K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is an extremal epimorphism from a spectral perfectoid algebra, so A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid; writing g♭ for the inverse system of the g^{1/p^k} modulo p one has g = #g♭.

items.name: Dense images, surjectivity and the canonical factorisation
items.statement: If φ:B→C has dense image and B is perfectoid then C is perfectoid; if moreover φ is surjective and B spectral, the spectral norm of C is the quotient norm and the induced map of unit balls is almost surjective. Hence φ is surjective iff φ♭ is, the condition being almost surjectivity of φ° mod ϖ, identified with φ♭° mod ϖ♭. Since ker φ♭ is a closed radicial ideal, B♭/ker φ♭ is perfectoid and φ factors in K-Perf as B → (B♭/ker φ♭)♯ → (B/ker φ)^u → C with the first surjective, the second simultaneously an extremal epimorphism in K-uBan and a monomorphism in K-Perf (different categories). André states these results are not used in the sequel.

items.name: The affinoid localization of K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩
items.statement: For char K = 0, taking ϖ of the form #(ϖ♭) and ϖ^{1/p^i} := #((ϖ♭)^{1/p^i}), the tilt of K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and one computes, level by level and in the completed colimit, K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}° = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞},(ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (3.12), the unit ball K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}_{≤1} = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞},ϖ^j/T⟩ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⊗̂_{K°⟨T⟩}K°⟨T,ϖ^j/T⟩ (3.13), and K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T} = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⊗̂_{K⟨T⟩}K⟨T⟩{ϖ^j/T} (3.14). By (3.12) this is perfectoid, hence uniform, but by (3.13) not spectral in general. For every uniform Banach K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra A with g the image of T, A{ϖ^j/g} ≅ A⊗̂_{K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩}K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T} (3.15).

items.name: Affinoid localizations of a perfectoid algebra at ϖ^j/g
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra with its spectral norm and g = T·1. For every j, A{ϖ^j/g} is perfectoid and (A°⊗̂_{K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩}K°⟨T^{1/p^∞},(ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩)_* ≅ A{ϖ^j/g}° (3.16); in particular A⊗̂_{K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩}K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/g}^u is spectral. For char K = 0, A{ϖ^j/g}♭ is identified with A♭{(ϖ♭)^j/g♭}.
items.note: The first clause is printed A{ϖ^j/T} and the rest A{ϖ^j/g}; since g = T·1 by hypothesis the mathematics is unaffected.

items.name: Rational localizations of a perfectoid algebra are perfectoid
items.statement: The same argument gives that A{f₁,…,f_n/g} is perfectoid whenever the f_i and g admit compatible systems of p^m-th roots; it is true without that hypothesis, Scholze deducing it by an approximation of f_i, g ∈ A° by elements #f̃_i♭, #g̃♭.

items.name: Uniform products and the Gelfand transform of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Uniform products of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid, because (∏A^{αo})/ϖ ≅ ∏(A^{αo}/ϖ). If A is perfectoid so is its Gelfand transform Γ(A), and Γ(A♭) ≅ Γ(A)♭: Γ(A) is a uniform product of the fields ℋ(x), each a uniform colimit of rational localizations of A hence perfectoid, and the second assertion follows from the commutation of rational localizations with tilting together with ℳ(A) ≅ ℳ(A♭). For A not perfectoid, Γ(A)♭ can be much larger than Γ(A♭), as for A = K⟨T⟩.

items.name: K-Perf is complete, and what its limits are
items.statement: The category of perfectoid K-algebras is complete, because K-uBan is complete and K-Perf is coreflective in it. In characteristic p the embedding also has a left adjoint and so preserves limits, with the indicated limits computed in K-uBan: perfectoid limits are the uniform limits, and ♭ commutes with ulim. In characteristic 0 one obtains them by tilting: perfectoid limits are ulim^♮.
items.ownershipReview: The cited stage does not establish this whole categorical contract. Provisional candidate in rejected route 2; no new owner is approved.

items.name: Perfectoid limits differ from uniform limits already for finite limits
items.statement: In characteristic 0 perfectoid and uniform limits do not coincide, already for finite limits: the intersection of two perfectoid subalgebras of a perfectoid algebra need not be perfectoid, as Â_∞[√g] = (completion of Q(A_∞))(√g) ∩ Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩ shows for p=2, n=1, g=T+4.

items.name: Invariants under an infinite group need not be perfectoid
items.statement: Proposition 3.8.1 does not extend to infinite groups: the Galois action of Z_p on T₁^{1/p^∞} extends by continuity to Â_∞, but the algebra A₀ of its invariants is not perfectoid.

items.name: The tilt of a perfectoid limit
items.statement: For char K = 0 with ϖ = #(ϖ♭), the perfectoid limit of a projective system of perfectoid K♭-algebras is their uniform limit. For a system of perfectoid K-algebras with uniform limit A, the perfectoid limit is A♮, whose tilt is determined by (A♮)^{♭o} = A^{♭o} = lim_F A° = lim_{F,α}A^{αo} = lim_α A^{α♭o} = lim_{F,α}(A^{αo}/ϖ) (3.17); A♮ → A is not an isomorphism in general.
items.note: The inverse limit of A° along x↦x^p in mixed characteristic is first a multiplicative-monoid construction. That power map is not additive on A°. The ring law is transported through the characteristic-p reduction description; do not implement an inverse system of mixed-characteristic rings with Frobenius ring maps.

items.name: A uniform limit of perfectoid algebras that is not perfectoid
items.statement: With p=2, n=1, g=T+4: by Théorème 4.2.2 the uniform limit of the Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩⟨ϖ^j/g⟩ is g^{−1/2^∞}Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩, the complete integral closure of Â_∞⟨g^{1/2^∞}⟩ in its localization at g; passing to 2Z₂-invariants, the uniform limit of the invariants is the complete integral closure of Â_∞[√g] in Â_∞[√g,1/g]. Since Â_∞ is completely integrally closed and the integral closure of a completely integrally closed ring in an algebraic extension of its fraction field is again completely integrally closed, that limit is Â_∞[√g], which is not perfectoid.
items.locator: Exemple prophylactique 3.8.5, p. 52; [8, ch. V, §1, ex. 14]

items.name: K-Perf is cocomplete
items.statement: The category of perfectoid K-algebras has filtered colimits, namely the uniform colimits, since Frobenius stays surjective on colim(B_α^{oa}/ϖ) ≅ (ucolim B_α)^{oa}/ϖ (3.18); having also amalgamated sums ⊗̂^u = ⊗̂, it is cocomplete, colimits being computed as in K-uBan and commuting with tilting.
items.ownershipReview: The cited stage does not establish this whole categorical contract. Provisional candidate in rejected route 2; no new owner is approved.

items.name: Completed algebraic extensions and infinite coproducts
items.statement: The completion of an algebraic extension of a perfectoid field K is the uniform colimit of the finite separable subextensions, each perfectoid, hence perfectoid. The coproduct of a family of perfectoid K-algebras is the completed tensor product ⊗̂_α B_α, and for every perfectoid B the morphism ⊗̂_{α∈B^{♭o}}K⟨T_α^{1/p^∞}⟩ → B, T_α ↦ #α, has dense image.

items.name: The p-adic Riemann extension theorem
items.statement: By the Riemann extension theorem bounded analytic functions on a complex polydisc minus a hypersurface g=0 extend to the polydisc; the p-adic analogue holds: with A = K₀°[[T₁,…,T_n]] = W(k)[[T_{≤n}]] and A₀ = A[1/p], one has A = lim_j A₀{ϖ^j/g}° (4.1) for every non-zero g∈A. Perfectoid versions of this statement are the object of §4.
items.locator: §4, opening, p. 53; [4] Bartenwerfer, quoted without a statement number

items.name: A short proof of the unit-ball form of the extension theorem
items.statement: The weaker statement A = lim_j A₀{ϖ^j/g}_{≤1} (4.2) has a short proof: after a change of variables one may take g in Weierstrass form in T_n, so that A/gA ≅ ⊕_{s<r}K₀°[[T_{<n}]]T_n^s and, by Nakayama, A = ⊕_s K₀°[[T_{<n},g]]T_n^s; applying ⊗_{K⟨g⟩_{≤1}}K⟨g,p^j/g⟩_{≤1} and killing p-primary torsion gives a compatible decomposition of A₀{p^j/g}_{≤1}, which reduces the claim to g = T_n, handled by expanding in powers of T_n. Passing to the uniform colimit to reach the perfectoid algebra Â_∞ "ne va pas de soi"; that is taken up in Exemple 4.2.6, where the equality with A₀{ϖ^j/g}° is also proved.
items.locator: §4.1, formula (4.2), p. 53; [8, VII, §3, n. 7 lemme 3 and n. 8 prop. 5]

items.name: Almost perfectoid envelopes of affinoid algebras
items.statement: Let B be a reduced affinoid K-algebra of dimension n. Choose a Noether normalisation making B a finite extension of A := K⟨T_{≤n}⟩, and choose g ∈ A° such that B[1/g] is étale over A[1/g]. Let 𝒜 be the almost perfectoid algebra g^{−1/p^∞}K⟨T_{≤n}^{1/p^∞},g^{1/p^∞}⟩ and let ℬ be the integral closure of B⊗_A𝒜 in B⊗_A𝒜[1/g]. Then ℬ is almost perfectoid by Proposition 5.3.1, and ℬ^{oa} is finite étale over 𝒜^{oa} modulo every power of p, in the setting (K°[T^{1/p^∞}],(ϖT)^{1/p^∞}K°[T^{1/p^∞}]) via T^{1/p^k} ↦ g^{1/p^k}. If Question 3.5.1 has a positive answer then 𝒜 and ℬ are even perfectoid. This constructs almost perfectoid envelopes, and conditionally perfectoid ones, for the specified reduced affinoid algebra and choices, where previous constructions were confined to toric situations governed by the logarithmic form of Faltings’ almost purity theorem.
items.note: The hypotheses are choices: the Noether normalisation, and an element g with B[1/g] étale over A[1/g], whose existence the paper does not argue here. The perfectoidness of 𝒜 and ℬ is conditional on Question 3.5.1 (p. 46), which the paper leaves open in characteristic 0. The tensor products are printed uncompleted.

items.name: Evaluation ideal of an almost module
items.statement: For an almost A-module P define E_{P/A} as the image of evaluation P⊗_A Hom_A(P,A)→A. It is an ideal; for almost projective P its equality to A characterizes faithful flatness. It is not defined by an endomorphism trace without finite-projectivity hypotheses.
items.locator: §1.7.2(1), p.7, corrected via Gabber–Ramero Definition 2.4.23 and Proposition 2.4.28(iv)
items.note: Required correction interface for E19.

items.name: Perfectoid monomorphisms detected after tilting
items.statement: A morphism of perfectoid K-algebras is a categorical monomorphism iff its tilt is injective. In characteristic p this is equivalent to underlying injectivity; in characteristic zero a categorical monomorphism need not be injective.

items.name: Noninjective monomorphism in mixed characteristic
items.statement: The evaluation K̂_cycl,∞⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩→L, where L is the completion of the extension adjoining compatible p-power roots of p and T maps to p, is not injective; its tilt is injective. It is therefore a categorical monomorphism of perfectoid algebras despite having a nonzero underlying kernel.
items.note: The cyclotomic base and compatible roots are part of the source example. This is distinct from Definition 3.5.2 on p.46.

items.name: Almost perfectoidness via the corrected left adjoint
items.statement: For a uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra B in the ramified almost setting, B is almost perfectoid iff the corrected left-adjoint representative (B^â)^!! is perfectoid. The hat on the corrected functor includes the topological construction of §2.3.

items.name: Integral characterization of almost perfectoid algebras
items.statement: In the ramified almost setting, A↦(A°)ᵃ identifies almost perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩^â-algebras with K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩°ᵃ-algebras flat over K°, ϖ-adically complete and with x↦x^p giving a bijection Aᵃ/ϖ^(1/p)→Aᵃ/ϖ. Keep the chosen compatible roots and almost base.

items.name: Finite étale equivalence over an almost perfectoid base
items.statement: For an almost perfectoid A, B↦(B°)ᵃ gives an equivalence between almost perfectoid A^â-algebras almost finite étale in the sense that Bᵃ is finite étale over Aᵃ, and finite étale (A°)ᵃ-algebras. Inversion of ϖ gives the inverse integral-to-Banach construction.
items.locator: Definition preceding Proposition 3.5.6 and Proposition 3.5.6, p.48

items.name: Topological power-bounded subring
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean commutative topological ring A, the power-bounded elements form the subring A°. This imports the topological carrier; identification of Huber boundedness with norm-bounded powers in the paper remains an explicit comparison.

items.name: Topologically nilpotent ideal in the power-bounded ring
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean commutative topological ring A, topologically nilpotent elements form an ideal of A°, not generally of A. Import this carrier before proving the paper's Banach-specific properties.

items.name: Ordinary integral closure as a subalgebra
items.statement: For commutative rings R,S and an R-algebra S, integralClosure R S is the subalgebra of elements integral over R. For the paper's inclusions use their induced algebra structure.

items.name: Algebraic integrality of a finite-group invariant extension
items.statement: If a finite group G acts on a commutative algebra B and every G-fixed element comes from A (Algebra.IsInvariant A B G), then B is integral over A. Apply to the invariant subring with the paper's inclusion; no norm invariance is required for this algebraic subresult.
items.note: MulSemiringAction.charpoly, charpoly_monic and charpoly_eval supply the orbit-polynomial proof; this is not an automatic spectral-norm invariance theorem.

sourceIssues.reason: Let F be the algebraic closure of Q_p inside C_p. It is dense and properly contained in C_p. Extend t from C_p minus F to a transcendence basis over F. The automorphism of the rational function field sending t to pt and fixing the other basis elements and F extends to an automorphism σ of its algebraic closure C_p. Thus ν(x)=|x| and ν′(x)=|σ(x)| are distinct complete multiplicative Q_p-algebra norms, with ν′(t)=p^(-1)ν(t). For a_n in F tending to t in ν, the same sequence tends to p^(-1)t in ν′. It is Cauchy for max(ν,ν′) but cannot have a limit for that norm. There is also an actual finite-group counterexample to the parenthesis of Lemme 2.4.1(2): put B=C_p×C_p with N(x,y)=max(ν(x),ν′(y)), let G=C_2 swap factors, and give A=B^G=diagonal C_p its induced norm max(ν,ν′). B is complete and spectral; A is uniform normed, exactly as allowed in §2.4.1, though incomplete. The swap takes (t,0), of norm ν(t), to (0,t), of norm p^(-1)ν(t). The proposed old repair from (2.11) is invalid: that formula determines max_γ N(γb), not N(b), and its proof of individual equality uses G-invariance. The prior extraction also missed the invocation on p.24. For a finite projective algebra over a complete A, its given complete Banach topology agrees with the canonical module topology: choose finite generators, use the continuous surjection A^n→B and open mapping. A-linear isomorphisms are then continuous, so fixed-topology uniqueness applies to p.24 and p.41. This does not repair the general parenthesis on p.22, where A need not be complete.

review.reason: Independently checked published pp.13,22,24,41 and Conrad's auxiliary theorem. Pullback by a wild automorphism of C_p fixing Q_p-bar gives different complete multiplicative norms; their maximum need not be complete. On C_p×C_p the transposition need not preserve max(ν(x),ν(σ(y))), disproving the automatic finite-group invariance as well. The original extraction's characteristic-polynomial repair is circular: part (3) already assumes invariance, and the orbit polynomial determines an orbit maximum, not each norm. Finite-projective topology supplies the separate continuity repair for the finite-étale application; no global downstream proof certification follows.

priorReview.reason: Checked the published text at all four locators and re-derived the counterexample. A wild automorphism σ of C_p over Q_p exists by extending a transcendence basis, and is discontinuous, hence non-isometric, so ν and ν∘σ are two distinct multiplicative — therefore spectral — Q_p-algebra norms for each of which C_p is complete (σ is an isometry (C_p,ν∘σ)→(C_p,ν)); the printed uniqueness claim of §2.2.4 p.13 is false. The finite-group counterexample to the parenthesis of Lemme 2.4.1(2) p.22 also holds as written: on B=C_p×C_p with N(x,y)=max(ν(x),ν∘σ(y)) — spectral because each factor norm is multiplicative, and complete — the transposition carries (t,0) of norm ν(t) to (0,t) of norm ν(σ(t)), and these differ for some t. I also checked the repair the entry proposes: continuity of each group element does suffice, since a continuous automorphism carries N to an equivalent spectral norm and the spectral radius lim‖f^n‖^(1/n) depends only on the topology; the transposition above is discontinuous, so it does not undercut that repair. The uses on p.24 and p.41 are as described, and the p.41 one is self-repairing because the text there also cites the fixed-topology form.

sourceIssues.correction: Every almost projective module is flat. Faithful flatness is equivalent to the evaluation ideal E_{P/A}=image(P⊗_A P*→A) being A; mere injectivity of A→End(P)ᵃ is insufficient in this generality. Use Gabber–Ramero Proposition 2.4.28(iv), with Definition 2.4.23, for this exact criterion.
sourceIssues.reason: Use the ordinary almost base (V,m)=(R,R), R=∏_{n∈N}F₂ and P=⊕_{n∈N}Re_n, the finite-support ideal. Each Re_n is projective, so P is projective; ann_R(P)=0, so it is faithful. But P²=P is proper, and P⊗_R(R/P)=P/P²=0 while R/P≠0. Hence P is not faithfully flat. The counterexample is infinite: no finite-coordinate computation is claimed to prove it. The cited Gabber–Ramero evaluation-ideal criterion and proof were read directly. This finding concerns the unrestricted sentence, not a claim that any particular almost-finite-projective downstream use is false.

sourceIssues.locator: Published numbered paragraph §2.2.2, p.13, displayed estimate in the uniformity equivalence
sourceIssues.correction: With C=sup_{b∈A°}‖b‖ and any c∈K with 0<|c|<1, the universally valid estimate is ‖a‖≤C|c|^(-1)|a|_sp. The sharp constant C is valid if |K×| is dense. Uniformity is still equivalent to equivalence with the spectral norm.
sourceIssues.reason: Take K=Q_p, A=Q_p(π) with π²=p, and the coefficient norm ‖a+bπ‖=max(|a|,|b|). It is normalized, complete and submultiplicative. Its spectral norm is max(|a|,p^(-1/2)|b|), since the two summands have valuations of different parity. Thus A°=Z_p+Z_pπ and C=1, but ‖π‖=1>p^(-1/2)=|π|_sp. For the repaired estimate choose scalar powers of c so that the rescaled spectral value is strictly below 1 and at least |c|; their powers are bounded, giving the stated constant. If the spectral value is zero, arbitrary scalar rescaling is power-bounded and boundedness of A° forces a=0. This refutes the auxiliary inequality, not the uniformity equivalence.
